text:
- chief complaint: annual exam.
- history of present illness: the patient reports worsening depression over the past year, attributed to prolonged isolation and stress, with partial benefit from Prozac 20 mg daily. Chronic back pain is aggravated by prolonged sitting and eased by movement. The patient had coronary artery bypass grafting early in life for a congenital heart condition and reports stable cardiac status.
- physical examination: no acute distress. No thyroid enlargement. Stable 3/6 systolic ejection murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Lumbar spine tenderness with decreased flexion. Lower extremity strength good, no edema. ECG and lumbar spine X-ray unchanged from last year.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: depressive symptoms, back stiffness and pain with prolonged sitting or standing, and mild numbness in the legs. No tingling, weakness, or radiating pain.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: Prozac increased from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Aspirin 81 mg daily continued.
- follow-up instructions: physical therapy referral and echocardiogram ordered. A nurse will contact the patient to schedule these.
